 B_N=A_{\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor}.$$ Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:bilateral_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:bilateral_limit">191</a> says that $B_N\to\infty$, that every sequence $N\to\infty$ has a further joint extraction of the bilateral contours and passage data, and that on this extraction the local rule is $\Lambda D_h$, for a deterministic $\Lambda$ in a fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. Brownian time is normalized to have total duration one; the deterministic factor from $N/2^{\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor}$ is included in $\Lambda$. We also use its uniform interval bound: if $I$ is an integer interval with $1\leq |I|\leq N$, and $\mathcal D(I)$ is its internal contour-vertex diameter, then $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_internal_bound}
 \big\|B_N^{-1}\mathcal D(I)\big\|_{L^k(\mathbb P)}
       \leq C\left(\frac{|I|}{N}\right)^s.$$ A bound with $|I|+1$ is equivalent here. These statements hold also on any fixed finite enlargement of the time window. No limit of adjacent normalizing ratios will be assumed.

<a id="pm-h-131"></a>
###### Conditioning and the additional passage data

<a id="stmt-tree-lem-excursion-density"></a>
<div id="tree:lem:excursion_density" class="lemma">

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound"></a>
<a id="tree:eq:sphere_return"></a>
<a id="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density"></a>
<a id="tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density"></a>
**Lemma 205** (Excursion densities). *There are constants $c,C>0$ such that, for all $m\geq0$ and $x\in\mathcal Q$, $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound}
 q_m(0,x)\leq C(x_1+1)(x_2+1)(m+1)^{-3}
                 \exp\left(-\frac{c|x|^2}{m+1}\right).$$ For positive even $N$, $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_return}
 q_N(0,0)\asymp (N+1)^{-3},\qquad
       \lim_{N\to\infty,\,N\text{ even}}N^3q_N(0,0)=\frac{32}{\pi}.$$ For $1\leq l\leq N/4$, the density of the increment path on $[l,2l]$ under $\mathbb P_N^{\mathrm{exc}}$, relative to the law of $l$ free increments, is $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density}
 f_{N,l}(\omega)=\frac{1}{q_N(0,0)}\sum_{x\in\mathcal Q}q_l(0,x)
  \mathbf1_{\{x+\omega_j\in\mathcal Q,\ 0\leq j\leq l\}}
                      q_{N-2l}(x+\Delta,0),\qquad \Delta=\omega_l.$$ It satisfies $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density}
 f_{N,l}(\omega)\leq C\prod_{i=1}^2
       \left(1+\frac{|\Delta_i|}{\sqrt l}\right)
       \leq C\left(1+\frac{|\Delta|}{\sqrt l}\right)^2,
 \qquad \sup_{N,l}\mathbb E[f_{N,l}^2]<\infty.$$*

*Fix $0<a<b<1$. The densities for the increment block $[\lfloor aN\rfloor,\lfloor bN\rfloor]$ converge, under the free invariance principle, to a continuous function of the limiting block’s coordinate minima and net increment. They are uniformly integrable, indeed uniformly bounded in $L^2$. Consequently, if arbitrary additional block-measurable passage data converge jointly with the free rescaled increments along a subsequence, their excursion-conditioned joint laws converge along that subsequence by the same change of density. Conditional on the limiting block increments, this change preserves their conditional kernel.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-tree-lem-excursion-density"><summary>Proof of stmt-tree-lem-excursion-density</summary>

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_reflection_1d"></a>
<a id="tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel"></a>
*Proof.* Let $p_r(h)$ be the simple symmetric one-dimensional walk transition probability from $0$ to $h$, and let $q_r^{(1)}$ denote its kernel killed on entering $-1$. Reflection gives, on the admissible parity lattice, $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_reflection_1d}
 q_r^{(1)}(0,h)=p_r(h)-p_r(h+2)
       =\frac{2(h+1)}{r+h+2}p_r(h),\qquad h\geq0.$$ The formula is interpreted directly at $r=0$ and at the ends of the walk’s support. The binomial formula for $p_r$, or Stirling’s inequalities, gives $$q_r^{(1)}(0,h)\leq C(h+1)(r+1)^{-3/2}
                    e^{-ch^2/(r+1)}.$$ Given the number $J$ of first-coordinate moves in $m$ steps, the two coordinate walks are independent and $J$ has the binomial law $\mathrm{Bin}(m,1/2)$. Thus $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel}
 q_m(0,x)=2^{-m}\sum_{j=0}^m\binom mj
                  q_j^{(1)}(0,x_1)q_{m-j}^{(1)}(0,x_2).$$ For $m/4\leq j\leq3m/4$, the preceding bound proves <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound]</a> term by term. The complementary binomial probability is at most $Ce^{-cm}$. On the support of $q_m(0,x)$, $|x|\leq m$; after decreasing $c$, this error is at most $C(m+1)^{-3}e^{-c|x|^2/(m+1)}$ and is absorbed in the same bound. The kernel is symmetric, so the bound also applies to $q_m(x,0)$.

Set $e_r=q_r^{(1)}(0,0)$. The exact formula is $e_{2j}=\binom{2j}{j}/(4^j(j+1))$, with $e_0=1$ and $e_{2j+1}=0$. Hence $e_r\sim 2^{3/2}\pi^{-1/2}r^{-3/2}$ through even $r$. Apply this to <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel">[tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel]</a> with $x=0$ and $m=N$. On $|J-N/2|\leq N^{3/4}$, the product of the two nonzero Catalan probabilities is $(64/\pi+o(1))N^{-3}$, uniformly. Exactly half the binomial mass is on even $J$; the mass outside this window is exponentially small compared with $N^{-3}$. This proves the limit in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_return" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_return">[tree:eq:sphere_return]</a>; increasing the constants covers all positive even $N$.

The Markov property at times $l$ and $2l$ proves <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density">[tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density]</a>. Since $N-2l\geq N/2$, use <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound]</a> twice and <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_return" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_return">[tree:eq:sphere_return]</a>. Drop the survival indicator and the exit Gaussian. Terms with $x+\Delta\notin\mathcal Q$ have zero weight, and for the other terms $x_i+\Delta_i+1\leq x_i+|\Delta_i|+1$. We obtain $$f_{N,l}(\omega)\leq C l^{-3}\prod_{i=1}^2
  \sum_{h\geq0}(h+1)(h+|\Delta_i|+1)e^{-ch^2/l}.$$ For $u\geq0$ and $l\geq1$, comparison with Gaussian integrals gives $$\sum_{h\geq0}(h+1)(h+u+1)e^{-ch^2/l}
       \leq C\big(l^{3/2}+ul\big).$$ This proves the pointwise bound in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density">[tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density]</a>. Free bounded increments have uniformly bounded moments of every fixed order after division by $\sqrt l$: expanding an even moment, every nonzero term pairs each independent centered increment with another occurrence of that increment, giving a bound $C_r l^r$ for the $2r$th moment. In particular the fourth moment proves the asserted $L^2$ bound. The same argument gives an $L^r$ bound for every fixed finite $r$.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt"></a>
Here are the local limits and the precise change-of-measure argument. They also fix all parity factors. Set $c_*=32/\pi$ and $$K_t(u)=c_* t^{-3}u_1u_2e^{-|u|^2/t},\qquad t>0,\quad u\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^2.$$ Extend $K_t$ by zero outside the quadrant, and use the same zero convention for killed kernels evaluated outside their state space. Uniformly when $t$ stays in a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$ and $x/\sqrt N$ stays in a fixed compact subset of the quadrant, Stirling’s formula in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_reflection_1d" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_reflection_1d">[tree:eq:sphere_reflection_1d]</a> and binomial concentration in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel">[tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel]</a> imply $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt}
 N^2q_{\lfloor tN\rfloor}(0,x)-K_t(x/\sqrt N)\longrightarrow0$$ on the admissible lattice $x_1+x_2\equiv\lfloor tN\rfloor\pmod2$. To check its coefficient, the one-dimensional local limit on its parity lattice is $p_j(h)\sim\sqrt{2/(\pi j)}e^{-h^2/(2j)}$. The product in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel">[tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel]</a>, with $j\sim tN/2$, therefore has coefficient $64/\pi$; its admissible binomial schedules have asymptotic mass $1/2$. Boundary points cause no problem for uniform absolute convergence: if one rescaled coordinate tends to zero, both sides of <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt]</a> tend to zero by <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound]</a>. This proves the stated uniform version.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_interior_density"></a>
Let $a_N=\lfloor aN\rfloor$, $b_N=\lfloor bN\rfloor$, and linearly interpolate a free block after dividing heights by $\sqrt N$ and times by $N$. For its limiting path $w$ of duration $b-a$, write $d=w(b-a)$ and $m_i=\min_t w_i(t)$. The limiting density is $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_interior_density}
 f_{a,b}(w)=\frac1{2c_*}\int_{\mathbb R_{\geq0}^2}
 K_a(u)K_{1-b}(u+d)
       \mathbf1_{\{u_i+m_i\geq0,\ i=1,2\}}\,du.$$ The discrete formula is <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density">[tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density]</a> with entrance length $a_N$, block length $b_N-a_N$, and exit length $N-b_N$. Each summation lattice has asymptotic density $N/2$ after rescaling; <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_return" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_return">[tree:eq:sphere_return]</a> and <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_lclt]</a> give <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_interior_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_interior_density">[tree:eq:sphere_interior_density]</a>. More explicitly, if rescaled paths $w_N$ converge uniformly to $w$, their minima and increments converge. On bounded $u$-sets the Riemann sums converge, since the boundaries $u_i=-m_i$ have zero Lebesgue measure. On their complements the Gaussian bound <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound]</a>, with bounded $d$, gives an integrable common majorant. It follows that $f_N(w_N)\to f_{a,b}(w)$. The same argument proves continuity of $f_{a,b}$ in the uniform path topology. Dropping the exit Gaussian as above also gives $$f_N(\omega)\leq C_{a,b}\left(1+\frac{|\Delta|}{\sqrt N}\right)^2.$$ Thus the densities are uniformly bounded in $L^2$ under the free law.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit"></a>
For completeness, suppose that $(W_N,H_N)$ denotes the rescaled free block together with any additional block data, taking values in the Polish data spaces of Proposition <a href="#tree:prop:certificate_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:prop:certificate_limit">175</a>, and that $(W_N,H_N)\Rightarrow(W,H)$. The preceding sequential convergence and uniform integrability imply, for every bounded continuous $\Phi$, $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit}
 \mathbb E\big[f_N(W_N)\Phi(W_N,H_N)\big]
       \longrightarrow \mathbb E\big[f_{a,b}(W)\Phi(W,H)\big].$$ Indeed, realize the unweighted convergence almost surely, truncate the densities at a fixed height, and then remove the truncation using their uniform $L^2$ bound. Taking $\Phi=1$ shows that the limiting density integrates to one. If the unweighted limit disintegrates as $\mu(dw)\mathsf K(w,dz)$, its weighted law is exactly $f_{a,b}(w)\mu(dw)\mathsf K(w,dz)$. This proves the assertion about additional data and their conditional kernel, not just convergence of the contour marginal. ◻

</details>

The corresponding full-contour invariance principle has a useful direct interpretation. Given a schedule with $J$ first-coordinate moves, excursion conditioning makes the two coordinate strings independent nonnegative bridges of lengths $J$ and $N-J$. The conditional mass of $J$ is <a id="tree:eq:sphere_schedule_excursion"></a>$$\label{tree:eq:sphere_schedule_excursion}
 \frac{2^{-N}\binom NJ e_Je_{N-J}}{q_N(0,0)}.$$ It is concentrated at $J/N=1/2$. For each $\epsilon>0$, the probability of $|J-N/2|>\epsilon N$ is at most $C N^3 e^{-c_\epsilon N}$, by the ordinary binomial bound and <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_return" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_return">[tree:eq:sphere_return]</a>. Conditional on $J$, all schedules are uniform and independent of the two coordinate bridges. Their partial counts satisfy $\sup_{r\leq N}|J_r-rJ/N|/N\to0$ in probability. One way to see the last assertion is to use $$\mathbb P[J_r=u\mid J]=\binom ru\binom{N-r}{J-u}\big/\binom NJ$$ and Stirling’s inequalities: for $J/N$ in a compact subset of $(0,1)$, the mass with $|u-rJ/N|>\epsilon N$ is at most $C N^C e^{-c_\epsilon N}$, uniformly in $r$; summing over $r$ suffices. Consequently the schedule time changes converge uniformly to half speed. The reflection formula gives the nonnegative-bridge finite-dimensional limits as the Brownian excursion transition densities. It also gives tightness: on a fixed interior time interval use the bounded $L^2$ density with respect to free increments; close to each endpoint use the one-dimensional version of <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density">[tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density]</a> and sum dyadic free-walk maximum bounds. The latter sum is bounded by $C\sum_{j\geq0}\sqrt{\delta2^{-j}}=C'\sqrt\delta$. This proves the excursion invariance principle, including the endpoints. Thus $N^{-1/2}Z^{\mathrm{disc}}_{\lfloor Nt\rfloor}$ converges to two independent Brownian excursions with the variance convention inherited from the axial walk.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint"></a>
By Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:background_peanosphere" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:background_peanosphere">167</a>, equivalently (Miller and Sheffield 2019, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-118"></a>[[MillerSheffieldSphere](#ref-MillerSheffieldSphere)], this pair encodes the area-one quantum sphere, with its area-parametrized space-filling $\mathrm{SLE}_8$. This is the ordinary sphere of (Duplantier, Miller, and Sheffield 2021, Definition 4.21(ii)) <a id="pm-cite-119"></a>[[DMS](#ref-DMS)]. Its distinguished points can be forgotten, by (Duplantier, Miller, and Sheffield 2021, Proposition A.13) <a id="pm-cite-120"></a>[[DMS](#ref-DMS)]; we write $q$ for the common point $\eta(0)=\eta(1)$ used by the encoding. The strict positivity of both excursions on $(0,1)$ gives $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint}
                      \eta^{-1}(\{q\})=\{0,1\}.$$ All deterministic Brownian boundary-length conventions here are the same ones as in the bilateral construction and Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:background_peanosphere" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:background_peanosphere">167</a>.

<a id="pm-h-132"></a>
###### The metric on interior sphere charts

<a id="stmt-tree-lem-sphere-interior-metric"></a>
<div id="tree:lem:sphere_interior_metric" class="lemma">

**Lemma 206** (Interior sphere metric). *In the joint extraction with distance units $B_N$ and deterministic multiplier $\Lambda$ selected above, the limiting finite-excursion local passage rule satisfies $$F_U(x,y)=\Lambda D_h(x,y;U)$$ for every buffered chart $U$ compactly contained in $S\setminus\{q\}$ and every $x,y$ joined by a path compactly in $U$. This identification retains the upper realization and lower subpath-extraction conclusions of Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:bilateral_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:bilateral_limit">191</a>.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-tree-lem-sphere-interior-metric"><summary>Proof of stmt-tree-lem-sphere-interior-metric</summary>

*Proof.* Fix rational $0<\delta<1/2$, and write $a=\delta$, $b=1-\delta$. Retain the complete collection of internal interval-chart passage data constructed solely from the increments on $[a_N,b_N]$. It includes every certificate whose range has positive clearance from the boundary of the interval surface, by Lemma <a href="#tree:lem:chart_reconstruction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:lem:chart_reconstruction">176</a>. Apply <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit">[tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit]</a> to this collection, first in finitely many compact charts and then by the countable extraction of Proposition <a href="#tree:prop:certificate_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:prop:certificate_limit">175</a>. In the bilateral reference law its compact-interior local passage rule equals $\Lambda D$, by Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:bilateral_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:bilateral_limit">191</a>; the equality event has probability one and is therefore preserved by the limiting density.

The restricted increments determine an abstract decorated quantum surface, including its quantum boundary-length units. For the cone this is (Gwynne, Holden, and Sun 2023, Lemma 4.9) <a id="pm-cite-121"></a>[[GHSSurvey](#ref-GHSSurvey)]. The sphere statement needed here is supplied separately by the final paragraph of the proof of (Miller and Sheffield 2019, Theorem 1.1, the case $\gamma\leq\sqrt2$, p. 49) <a id="pm-cite-122"></a>[[MillerSheffieldSphere](#ref-MillerSheffieldSphere)]: conditionally on the contour values at $\delta$ and $1-\delta$, the quantum surface complementary to $\eta([0,\delta])\cup\eta([1-\delta,1])$ has the corresponding cone conditional law and is determined, together with its curve, by the restricted contour. This is the symmetric interval statement recorded in Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:background_peanosphere" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:background_peanosphere">167</a>. Its quantum units agree with those in the density calculation. Metric locality and conformal covariance therefore identify its internal $D$ with the internal metric on its image in the area-one sphere. The transported equality is an equality with this sphere’s $D_h$ in the fixed normalization.

This equality is an event of the restricted contour and its passage data, since those contour increments determine the abstract interval surface. Adjoining the outside contour therefore preserves the same probability-one equality.

Finally, if $K\subset S\setminus\{q\}$ is compact, continuity of $\eta$ and <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint">[tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint]</a> imply that $\eta^{-1}(K)$ is contained in $(\delta,1-\delta)$ for some rational $0<\delta<1/2$. Choose a smaller positive rational $\delta$ if necessary. The image of the omitted compact time intervals is disjoint from $K$, so $K$ lies in the interior of the interval surface and has positive spatial clearance from its boundary. Its local certificates are therefore among the ones just transferred. By a countable exhaustion, the local passage rule off $q$ equals $\Lambda D_h$ simultaneously in these charts, with the same deterministic $\Lambda$. ◻

</details>

We also record how the transfer behaves when the complete outside contour is retained. The following conditional-kernel statement allows the inside passage observations to be used jointly with outside contour observations.

<a id="stmt-tree-lem-sphere-exterior-kernel"></a>
<div id="tree:lem:sphere_exterior_kernel" class="lemma">

**Lemma 207** (The kernel after adjoining the outside contour). *Fix $0<a<b<1$. In the setup of Equation <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit">[tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit]</a>, suppose the free joint limit of the block increments $W_N$ and block-measurable passage data $H_N$ disintegrates as $\mu(dw)\mathsf K(w,dz)$. Write $W,H$ for the corresponding interior increment path and passage datum in their joint excursion-conditioned limit with the complete contour. The conditional law of $H$ given that contour is $\mathsf K(W,\cdot)$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-tree-lem-sphere-exterior-kernel"><summary>Proof of stmt-tree-lem-sphere-exterior-kernel</summary>

*Proof.* The assertion follows from the Markov factorization: given the entrance height $x$ and the inside increments, the outside consists of a killed entrance bridge and a killed exit bridge, independent of the inside data. Their weights are the two factors in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density">[tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_density]</a>. On compact positive-height ranges, the reflection formula for $q_m(x,y)$ (the four coordinate reflections of the free two-dimensional kernel) gives uniform bridge finite-dimensional limits. For tightness at the zero endpoint, the one-dimensional reflection formula gives $q_r^{(1)}(u,v)\leq C(u+1)(v+1)(r+1)^{-3/2}$: telescope step-two differences of $p_r$ in the smaller of $u,v$, using symmetry of the kernel and the binomial Gaussian bound. Averaging over schedules as in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel">[tree:eq:sphere_schedule_kernel]</a> consequently gives $q_m(y,z)\leq C_R(y_1+1)(y_2+1)N^{-2}$ when $m\asymp N$ and $|z|\leq R\sqrt N$. On a fixed positive-height compact set, $q_{a_N}(0,z)\geq c_RN^{-2}$, so the proof of <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density">[tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density]</a> applies to the small dyadic blocks of this entrance bridge. At its other endpoint, reverse the bridge: the increment density on an initial short block is bounded by $C_R(1+|\Delta|/\sqrt N)^2$, using <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound]</a>. Free-walk maximum bounds therefore give tightness there too. This proves the uniform bridge convergence used here.

Both entrance and exit heights can be restricted to positive compact sets before this calculation. Indeed their marginal law at time $j$ is $$\mathbb P_N^{\mathrm{exc}}[Z_j^{\mathrm{disc}}=x]
       =\frac{q_j(0,x)q_{N-j}(x,0)}{q_N(0,0)}.$$ Uniformly for $j/N$ in a compact subinterval of $(0,1)$, <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_entrance_bound]</a> bounds this by $CN^{-3}(x_1+1)^2\allowbreak\mbox{$(x_2+1)^2$}e^{-c|x|^2/N}$. Summing shows that the probability of either coordinate below $\epsilon\sqrt N$ has limsup at most $C\epsilon^3$, whereas the probability of $|x|>R\sqrt N$ tends to zero uniformly as $R\to\infty$. Apply these bounds at both $a_N$ and $b_N$.

Retain the rescaled entrance height $u=x/\sqrt N$ jointly in the Riemann sum proving <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit">[tree:eq:sphere_weighted_joint_limit]</a>. On the preceding compact sets, the two bridge kernels converge uniformly and are independent of the additional inside data given $(u,w)$. The limiting joint law consequently has the form $$\mu(dw)\mathsf K(w,dz)\,
 \frac{K_a(u)K_{1-b}(u+d)}{2c_*}
 \mathbf1_{\{u_i+m_i\geq0,\ i=1,2\}}\,du\,
 \mathsf B_a(0,u;d\omega^-)\mathsf B_{1-b}(u+d,0;d\omega^+),$$ where $\mathsf B$ are the limiting killed bridge laws. The marginal tail bounds just proved remove the truncations. Conditioning on the complete contour $(\omega^-,w,\omega^+)$ therefore leaves the inside kernel $\mathsf K(w,dz)$ unchanged, exactly as in Lemma <a href="#tree:lem:finite_kernel_transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:lem:finite_kernel_transfer">178</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-133"></a>
###### Endpoint diameters

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_block"></a>
The density estimate controls the metric information which an interior change of measure cannot see. Let $v_i$ be the primal vertex at contour time $i$, with $v_0=v_N$, and set $$T_N(\delta)=\{v_i:0\leq i\leq\lfloor\delta N\rfloor
                   \text{ or }N-\lfloor\delta N\rfloor\leq i\leq N\}.$$ For $1\leq l\leq N/4$, Cauchy–Schwarz, <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density">[tree:eq:sphere_polynomial_density]</a>, and <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_internal_bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_internal_bound">[tree:eq:sphere_internal_bound]</a> give $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_block}
 \mathbb E_N^{\mathrm{exc}}\left[B_N^{-1}\mathcal D([l,2l])\right]
 \leq \|f_{N,l}\|_2
         \left\|B_N^{-1}\mathcal D([0,l])\right\|_2
 \leq C(l/N)^s.$$ The internal distances in this display are genuine functions of the block increments, so the density calculation applies to them exactly. If only endpoint norms are used in Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:bilateral_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:bilateral_limit">191</a>, the diameter bound follows by balanced binary subdivision: at depth $r$, the maximum of at most $2^r$ endpoint costs has $L^k$ norm at most $C(l/N)^s2^{-r(s-1/k)}$ in $B_N$ units; summing these bounds is finite since $s>1/k$. Rounded subdivision lengths change the constant only.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes_probability"></a>
For $0<\delta\leq1/8$ and $\delta N\geq1$, choose $J$ with $2^J\leq\delta N<2^{J+1}$. The chain $$[0,1],\ [1,2],\ [2,4],\ldots,\ [2^J,2^{J+1}]$$ covers $[0,\delta N]$ and its consecutive intervals share endpoints. Every block except $[0,1]$ in this chain satisfies the hypothesis of <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_block" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_block">[tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_block]</a>. Its first interval has graph diameter at most one. Connect points through the common endpoints using the interval paths and sum the resulting diameter bounds. Time reversal gives the same bound at $N$, and the two chains meet at $v_0=v_N$. If $\delta N<1$, the endpoint set consists only of this vertex. We have proved <a id="tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes"></a>$$\label{tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes}
 \mathbb E_N^{\mathrm{exc}}\left[B_N^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{d_n}T_N(\delta)\right]
       \leq C\delta^s+2B_N^{-1},\qquad 0<\delta\leq1/8.$$ In particular, $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes_probability}
 \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \mathbb P_N^{\mathrm{exc}}\left[
       B_N^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{d_n}T_N(\delta)>\epsilon\right]=0
       \quad\text{for every }\epsilon>0.$$ This is an estimate for the actual ambient graph metric; the internal metrics appeared only to construct admissible paths.

On a closed interior time interval, the uniform $L^2$ density in Lemma <a href="#tree:lem:excursion_density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:lem:excursion_density">205</a> transfers the free time-modulus estimate of Lemma <a href="#tree:lem:moment_compactness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:lem:moment_compactness">172</a>. Explicitly, if an event has free probability $r$, its conditioned probability is at most $C_{a,b}\sqrt r$. Together with <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes_probability" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes_probability">[tree:eq:sphere_no_spikes_probability]</a>, this gives tightness of the cyclic time modulus of the rescaled ambient distances on $[0,1]$. Indeed first cover $[\delta,1-\delta]$ by finitely many interior blocks, and then join its ends to the two endpoint chains just constructed. The same argument bounds the full diameter in probability.

<a id="pm-h-134"></a>
###### Identification of unrestricted distances

<a id="stmt-tree-lem-tour-measure"></a>
<div id="tree:lem:tour_measure" class="lemma">

<a id="tree:eq:tour_degree"></a>
**Lemma 208** (The measure counted by the tree tour). *Let $v_i$ be the primal vertex represented by contour time $i$, with $v_N=v_0$. Then, for every $v\in V(M_n)$, $$\label{tree:eq:tour_degree}
 \#\{0\leq i<N:v_i=v\}=\deg_{M_n}(v).$$ Consequently, if $$\mu_n=\frac1{2n}\sum_{v\in V(M_n)}\deg_{M_n}(v)\,\delta_v,
 \qquad f_n(t)=v_{\lfloor Nt\rfloor},\quad 0\leq t\leq1,$$ then $(f_n)_*\mathrm{Leb}_{[0,1]}=\mu_n$. Conditional on the map, independent uniform times give independent samples from $\mu_n$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-tree-lem-tour-measure"><summary>Proof of stmt-tree-lem-tour-measure</summary>

*Proof.* Associate time slot $i\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ with the step departing at $i$. The two horizontal traversals of a tree edge depart once from each endpoint, so these slots count its two incidences. Every vertical step belongs to a unique matched pair with terminal times $u<v$. By <a href="#tree:eq:discrete_R_match" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:discrete_R_match">[tree:eq:discrete_R_match]</a>, this pair adds a non-tree edge between $v_{u-1}$ and $v_{v-1}$; its two departure slots count exactly those two incidences. This also counts a loop twice. Every slot belongs to exactly one such pair, proving <a href="#tree:eq:tour_degree" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:tour_degree">[tree:eq:tour_degree]</a>. Each slot has time mass $1/N=1/(2n)$, which proves the pushforward identity and the sampling assertion. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-tree-prop-sphere-identification"></a>
<div id="tree:prop:sphere_identification" class="proposition">

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_preliminary_limit"></a>
**Proposition 209** (Sphere identification). *For every sequence of positive integers $n\to\infty$, there is a further subsequence and a deterministic $\Lambda\in(0,\infty)$ such that $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_preliminary_limit}
        (V(M_n),B_{2n}^{-1}d_n,\mu_n)
              \ \Rightarrow\ (S,\Lambda D_h,\mu_h)$$ in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology. The constants $\Lambda$ lie in a fixed deterministic compact subset of $(0,\infty)$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-tree-prop-sphere-identification"><summary>Proof of stmt-tree-prop-sphere-identification</summary>

*Proof.* Choose a simultaneous bilateral extraction as in Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:bilateral_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:bilateral_limit">191</a>, with its deterministic multiplier $\Lambda$. Lemma <a href="#tree:lem:sphere_interior_metric" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:lem:sphere_interior_metric">206</a> gives convergent sphere certificates on every compact subset of $S\setminus\{q\}$, with local passage rule $\Lambda D_h$. The local certificate assertions include realization with open margins, subpath extraction, and uniformly negligible costs for joining nearby endpoints.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification"></a>
We give the compactness and path argument explicitly. Put $$\rho_N(t,u)=B_N^{-1}d_n(v_{\lfloor Nt\rfloor},v_{\lfloor Nu\rfloor}),
                    \qquad 0\leq t,u\leq1.$$ Consecutive contour vertices are equal or joined by a tree edge, so replacing $\rho_N$ by its bilinear interpolation changes it by at most $2/B_N$. The cyclic time modulus and diameter bound proved above imply tightness of these interpolations in $C([0,1]^2)$. Extract jointly with the contours and all certificate charts, and use an almost sure representation. Then $\rho_N$ converges uniformly to a continuous pseudometric $\rho$ on $[0,1]$, with $\rho(0,1)=0$. The limiting contour determines the sphere and its continuous surjection $\eta$. In particular the endpoint time sets have limiting $\rho$-diameters tending to zero. We will show that $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification}
                       \rho(t,u)=\Lambda D_h(\eta(t),\eta(u))
                       \quad(0\leq t,u\leq1).$$

The projection part of Proposition <a href="#tree:prop:certificate_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:prop:certificate_limit">175</a> applies to the finite excursion sewing as well: its proof uses uniform contour convergence and the defining link relations. Thus all representatives of a single vertex have $D_h$-close images, uniformly over vertices, and the two endpoints of every graph edge have $D_h$-distance tending to zero, uniformly over edges. To see the uniform assertion directly, a contrary sequence has convergent contour times; the limiting tree identification or matched second-coordinate chord identifies the two images. This also covers links involving time $0$ or $1$, which project to $q$. Choose any representative of each vertex and write $\pi_N(v)$ for its image under $\eta$ at the rescaled time. Let $\varepsilon_N\to0$ bound both representative errors and edge-image jumps. These maps are only used to locate paths in the limiting surface; all costs remain discrete all-edge costs.

We first record a uniform local crossing fact. If $K\subset S\setminus\{q\}$ is compact, take finitely many pairs of open sets $V_i\Subset U_i$ covering $K$, all contained in interval-surface interiors. Choose $r>0$ so small that every $D_h$-ball of radius $3r$ about a point of $K$ is contained in one of the $U_i$ with positive clearance from its boundary. A discrete path beginning at such a point, stopped on first reaching $D_h$-displacement $r$, stays in that compact chart after an $\varepsilon_N$ enlargement. For all sufficiently large $N$, it has scaled cost at least $\Lambda r/2$. Otherwise a subsequence of these paths has bounded cost and compact confinement; subpath extraction gives a certificate with endpoints at distance $r$ and cost at most $\Lambda r/2$, contradicting the local lower comparison. Compactness of $K$ and the finite cover make this assertion uniform in its starting point and in the path. Paths of larger cost already satisfy it. It follows that a path of scaled cost at most $L$ can be divided into at most $2L/(\Lambda r)+2$ such steps, with a final shorter step, as long as it stays in $K$.

For the upper bound in <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification">[tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification]</a>, fix $t,u$ and a $D_h$-geodesic $P$ from $x=\eta(t)$ to $y=\eta(u)$. A compact subarc disjoint from $q$ has a finite subdivision into pieces lying with open margins in the sets $U_i$ of a finite local cover. For each piece the local upper comparison and realization supply approximating discrete paths with cost at most $\Lambda$ times that piece’s $D_h$-length, plus an arbitrarily prescribed positive error. Uniform joining connects their endpoints, also with vanishing cost. Consequently a geodesic whose range avoids $q$ gives $\rho(t,u)\leq\Lambda D_h(x,y)$.

<a id="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_ball"></a>
Here is the endpoint modification when $P$ meets $q$, also valid if one or both endpoints are $q$. Given $\delta>0$, compactness and <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint">[tree:eq:sphere_single_endpoint]</a> give a radius $r_\delta>0$ such that $$\label{tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_ball}
 \eta^{-1}(\overline B_{D_h}(q,2r_\delta))
                         \subset[0,\delta)\cup(1-\delta,1].$$ If $P$ enters $B_{D_h}(q,r_\delta)$, retain its portion before the first entry and its portion after the last exit. Both are compactly away from $q$ except for their retained endpoints, which are still at positive distance from $q$ unless the whole portion is empty. Apply the finite local subdivision to these portions. The two cut endpoints have contour representatives in the endpoint time set of <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_ball" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_ball">[tree:eq:sphere_endpoint_ball]</a>. Their approximating vertices can be connected at cost at most the scaled diameter of $T_N(\delta)$, with a vanishing joining error; the same applies if an original endpoint lies in this set. The sum of the retained geodesic lengths is at most $D_h(x,y)$. Uniform convergence of $\rho_N$ therefore gives $$\rho(t,u)\leq\Lambda D_h(x,y)+
       \mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_\rho([0,\delta]\cup[1-\delta,1]).$$ The last term tends to zero by continuity of $\rho$ at $0$ and $1$. This proves the upper bound in all cases.

For the lower bound, choose shortest discrete paths between the two contour vertices. Their scaled lengths converge to $\rho(t,u)$ and are bounded. Fix $r>0$. If a path has vertices whose images lie in $B_{D_h}(q,r)$, remove the portion between its first and last such vertices, retaining its prefix and suffix. The removed portion has nonnegative cost. Its two cut endpoints have $D_h$-distance at most $2r$. Apart from these endpoints, the retained pieces stay outside $B_{D_h}(q,r)$; since edge-image jumps are at most $\varepsilon_N$, they are contained in $S\setminus B_{D_h}(q,r/2)$ for large $N$. If there is no visit, retain the entire path. Cases with an endpoint inside the ball simply have an empty retained piece.

Cover $S\setminus B_{D_h}(q,r/2)$ by the finite buffered local charts above and choose a fixed step size $r'>0$ for that cover. Divide each retained piece at successive first $D_h$-displacements $r'$. The uniform crossing fact bounds the number of pieces independently of $N$. Pass to a further extraction recording their endpoints, costs, and marked subpaths. Each piece has a limiting certificate compactly in one chart. Its limiting cost is at least $\Lambda$ times its endpoints’ $D_h$-distance. Add these inequalities, including the final shorter pieces. The triangle inequality in $D_h$ then gives $$\rho(t,u)\geq \Lambda\big(D_h(x,y)-2r\big).$$ No cost is assigned to the removed segment in this bound. Letting $r\downarrow0$ proves the required lower inequality. In particular, it rules out a short global path escaping a local chart and returning at a different point; such a path has paid for its successive chart crossings. We have proved <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification">[tree:eq:sphere_uniform_identification]</a>.

The construction applies first on a countable dense set of contour pairs. Continuity of $\rho$, $D_h$, and $\eta$ extends it to every pair. As $\rho_N\to\rho$ uniformly, the correspondence $$\mathcal R_N=\{(v_{\lfloor Nt\rfloor},\eta(t)):0\leq t\leq1\}$$ has distortion tending to zero when the discrete metric is $B_N^{-1}d_n$ and the sphere metric is $\Lambda D_h$. It covers both spaces: every primal vertex has a contour visit and $\eta$ is surjective. Moreover, Lemma <a href="#tree:lem:tour_measure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:lem:tour_measure">208</a> gives $(f_n)_*\mathrm{Leb}=\mu_n$, and quantum-area parametrization gives $\eta_*\mathrm{Leb}=\mu_h$. Lemma <a href="#measure:parameter" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="measure:parameter">4</a> therefore bounds the GHP distance by half the same distortion. This proves <a href="#tree:eq:sphere_preliminary_limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:eq:sphere_preliminary_limit">[tree:eq:sphere_preliminary_limit]</a>. The bounds and deterministic nature of $\Lambda$ come from Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:bilateral_limit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:bilateral_limit">191</a>; a change of density cannot change a fixed almost sure equality constant. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-135"></a>
###### A deterministic normalization for every integer

<details id="proof-stmt-tree-prop-sphere-identification-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-tree-prop-sphere-identification</summary>

*Proof of the spanning-tree case of Theorem <a href="#tree:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:thm:main">1</a>.* Let $X=\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{D_h}S$. The ordinary area-one quantum sphere is compact and nontrivial, so $0<X<\infty$ almost surely. With the center $m$ from Lemma <a href="#measure:center" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="measure:center">[measure:center]</a>, define, for every positive integer $n$, <a id="tree:eq:sphere_final_normalization"></a>$$\label{tree:eq:sphere_final_normalization}
 X_n=\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{d_n}V(M_n),\qquad
 a_n=\exp\left\{m(\log X)-m\big(\log(X_n\vee1)\big)\right\}.$$ These are positive deterministic constants; the truncation includes one-vertex maps. Proposition <a href="#tree:prop:sphere_identification" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tree:prop:sphere_identification">209</a> supplies every hypothesis of Lemma <a href="#measure:normalization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="measure:normalization">6</a>, with $s_n=B_{2n}\to\infty$ and a deterministic positive subsequential multiplier $\Lambda$. Hence $a_n\to0$ and $$(V(M_n),a_nd_n,\mu_n)\Longrightarrow(S,D_h,\mu_h)$$ in GHP topology along all positive integers. All distances use every primal edge, and forgetting the root and spanning tree gives the unmarked metric probability spaces in the theorem. ◻

</details>
